gaps.sentence: 'I saw her yesterday,' she said. She said she had seen her ___.
gaps.explanation: Yesterday becomes the day before (or the previous day) in reported speech.

gaps.sentence: 'I'm looking for a flat near the hospital,' she explained. She explained that she ___ for a flat near the hospital.
gaps.explanation: Present continuous becomes past continuous in reported speech: was looking.

gaps.sentence: "Congratulations!" — She ___ me on passing the exam.
'Have you seen my reading glasses?' he asked. He asked ___ his reading glasses.
gaps.explanation: 'If/whether' reports a yes/no question; the tense backshifts to past perfect.
'Whether/if' + statement order + 'had' for the present perfect.

gaps.sentence: 'It was your team that missed the deadline,' the director told us. The director ___ missing the deadline.
gaps.explanation: 'Blame somebody for something' is the correct pattern; 'accuse' takes 'of'.

gaps.sentence: 'I've been studying all night,' she said. She said she ___ studying all night.
gaps.hint: present perfect continuous → past perfect continuous
gaps.explanation: have been + -ing backshifts to had been + -ing.

gaps.sentence: 'We may be a few minutes late,' they warned. They warned that they ___ be a few minutes late.
